chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who prostrates: how many tasbihs (glorifications) suffice for him in his bowing and prostration? He said: 'Three, and one suffices for him.'

key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: Suffices for him / is accepted as valid

ai.seo_question: How many times must one recite tasbih in ruku and sujud for the prayer to be valid?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the obligatory minimum (wajib) and the recommended perfection (mustahabb) of glorifications in prayer, establishing that while three repetitions are ideal, a single recitation suffices for validity. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of leniency in the essential acts of worship, ensuring the prayer's validity even with minimal recitation while encouraging greater devotion. It highlights the practical flexibility in fiqh that accommodates both the hurried and the devout worshipper.
